change: the coverage ledger is now a mandatory verification artefact, enforced by registry.datasets_without_coverage_ledger() and reported by ds-registry
why: the ledger has twice found coverage movement that careful reading of a narrative did not - four surfaces silently un-resolved by DS-ACT-INHOUSE, and INV-D02 silently activated by DS-ACT-VOIDCN on a dataset whose every expectation passed. A dataset can be COMMISSIONED and still cover less than production did: commissioning asks whether the declared outcomes are right, only the ledger asks what the dataset can exercise at all.

design.per_dataset_recency: every retained pack is read newest-first and the most recent one NAMING a dataset decides it. A ledger is per-dataset, unlike commissioning which runs the whole registry at once, so taking simply the latest pack would condemn every dataset but the one measured last.
design.pack_matching: containment, not suffix - ds-coverage writes {timestamp}_ds_coverage_{tag} and only when --tag is given. Not a guess: the suffix form was the defect this registry shipped with, found on the first dataset to declare COMMISSIONED.

commissioning: 8 checks, 0 failed, against fabricated evidence directories
cases: no ledgers on the machine flags every dataset
a passing ledger for each backs them all
an UNDECLARED_MOVEMENT ledger flags its dataset - the case the gate exists for
a later passing ledger supersedes an earlier failure
a later failure supersedes an earlier pass
one dataset ledger does not cover the others
a ds_commission pack is not read as a ledger
a pack with no result.json backs nothing
